hypothesis: Increasing only canonical HYPE breakout notional from $25 to $75 at unchanged 5x isolated leverage may improve research information and absolute returns without materially degrading execution friction.
decision: Preserve the evidence-routed $75 profile as an inactive candidate. Do not stage or activate it automatically. Because this exact candidate also changes HYPE to a fixed eight-hour exit, treat any future run as a joint allocation-and-exit experiment unless those variables are separated before activation.
falsifier: Profile-matched HYPE profit factor at or below one, negative after-cost PnL over twenty to thirty closes, material outcome concentration, incomplete visible $75 depth, or realized entry and exit friction materially worse than the $25 sample would falsify the allocation hypothesis.
limitations: The six-close live HYPE sample is insufficient to establish durable edge at either allocation.
The candidate changes allocation and exit policy together, confounding causal attribution.
Displayed public depth can cancel before an IOC reaches the venue.
The candidate is neither staged nor active and has no signing authority.
